title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a governance failure inside a communications workflow, not a failure of the image model itself. The tool did what such tools do, and the harm came from where it was pointed: a real student's likeness was replaced with a generated person and the resulting image was published on campus banners as a photograph of a Stanford event. The university's own policy already barred AI from producing or altering images of Stanford people and events, so the rule existed before the image was made and was not applied to it.

Catching this required a review step between editing and publication, one that compared the altered file against the existing policy and asked whether the people depicted had consented to a fabricated version of themselves. The university has said it is now arranging additional training and proper review of materials, which describes the check that was absent. Nothing in the facts shows a technical safeguard that failed, only a human approval that did not happen.

It is not established who performed the alteration, at whose direction, or with what intent, and Stanford's acknowledgement covers the policy violation rather than anyone's motive.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
Stanford used artificial intelligence to alter a photo on campus banners. In the original 2024 photo, Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology, stood with two other students at a Lunar New Year party. The university's dining service posted it online. When Stanford used the image on banners last week, Ramirez had been replaced by an image of a Black woman, and the other students were made to look thinner. Ramirez learned about the change from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated.

Stanford acknowledged on Tuesday that it had used artificial intelligence to change the original image. It said its policy bans artificial intelligence use in producing or altering images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. The alteration and lack of disclosure violated that policy. Stanford said it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide additional training and ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
